title: Approval TTL & Revocation Playbook — PRD draft
body:
Status: draft — rough PRD for Approval TTL (time-to-live) and Revocation semantics for customer-managed networking / private deployments.

Overview:
This doc proposes a practical, operator-friendly approach to timebound approvals and revocation propagation for customer-managed networking changes (VPC on-prem edge connectors, ephemeral tunnels, peering changes). The goal is to provide: a) short-lived approvals with cryptographic proof and TTLs, b) clear revocation semantics that propagate through monitoring/forensics, and c) audit evidence bundles that are small, queryable, and useful for customers and Redwood ops.

Why: we've had repeated asks from customers and SRE for: faster approvals for emergency ops, machine-initiated temporary approvals for integration tests, and stronger guarantees that revoked approvals cannot be reused. Existing approval ledger work covers immutable signing and long-term retention; this complements that by focusing on expirations and active revocation flows.

Goals:
- Define an Approval Token model: opaque token issued by Redwood control-plane with TTL, signature, scope (route-level, vpc-level), and revocation handle.
- Define Revocation API: immediate revocation endpoint + asynchronous propagation to edge operators and telemetry collectors.
- Audit Evidence Bundle: compact JSON-LD-ish summary for each approval/revocation with links to full logs (S3/siem), hashes, and operator annotations.
- UX & Operators: lightweight UI for issuing ephemeral approvals, revoking them, and seeing traces (who/when/why).
- Compliance: retention and export options to match customer policies (90 / 365 / per-jurisdiction).

Non-goals:
- Replacing the immutable audit ledger — this builds on top of that.
- Designing new crypto primitives beyond standard signing + HMAC.

Functional requirements (high level):
1) IssueApproval(scope, subject, ttl_seconds, reason) -> ApprovalToken (base64)
   - Scope syntax: vpc:<id>:route:<cidr> | edge-connector:<id> | global:customer:<id>.
   - Tokens include: token_id, issued_at, expires_at, issuer_id, scope, signature, revocation_endpoint.
2) RevokeApproval(token_id, requestor_id, reason) -> 200/202; writes revocation record to ledger; returns revocation_receipt with timestamp and proof hash.
3) Validate(token, target) -> PASS/FAIL + failure_reason. Validation must verify signature, TTL, scope match, and revocation status.
4) Propagation: revocation must be pushed to online edge controllers (webhook/stream) and to downstream telemetry exporters (siem, splunk, customer-s3).

Audit/evidence requirements:
- Evidence bundle (small): {token_id, token_hash, issued_by, issued_at, expires_at, scope, reason, revocation_status, revocation_by, revocation_at, related_change_ids} plus pointer to full log. Must be < 4 KB per event by default.
- Full logs: raw operator events, network traces, API request records — stored per customer retention policy.
- Indexing keys: token_id, customer_id, scope, operator_id, change_id, timestamp for fast queries in Console.

Revocation semantics (detailed):
- Immediate revocation: API call creates revocation record with revocation_at and revocation_receipt. Control-plane marks token state=REVOKED.
- Propagation modes (best-effort / acked):
   a) Best-effort push: HTTP webhook to edge controllers; if failed, control-plane retries x backoff.
   b) Acknowledged: for dedicated customers who opt-in, edge controllers must ACK revocation within 5s or mark degraded.
- Fail-open vs Fail-closed: default for non-critical routes: fail-open for latency-sensitive infra. For admin/scoped actions (e.g., GH secrets upload, key escrow), require fail-closed. Make policy configurable per-customer.
- Revocation window: even after token expires, an explicit revocation record must be stored (to prove operator action).

APIs & contracts (notes to eng):
- POST /v1/approvals -> returns token object. Authentication via existing customer tokens. Rate-limit: 100/min per customer.
- POST /v1/approvals/{token_id}/revoke -> returns revocation_receipt. Must be idempotent.
- GET /v1/approvals/{token_id}/status -> returns current state and evidence bundle pointer.
- POST /v1/approvals/validate -> used by edge controllers; lightweight response schema for in-band checks.
- Webhook: POST to customer-supplied URL or internal edge subscriber: payload includes token_id, token_hash, revocation_receipt, scope, revocation_at. Must be signed and include replay-protection nonce.

Operator console / UX sketches (bullet notes):
- Single-line issue box: scope + TTL dropdown (15m,1h,6h,custom up to 72h) + reason + who (link to slack thread).
- Active approvals table: filters by scope/customer/operator. Actions: revoke, extend TTL (requires re-approval flow), annotate.
- Revocation audit view: show revocation receipts, propagation status (acked / pending / failed), recent retry logs.
- Lightweight mobile action for emergency revoke (2FA required for >30m TTL or for certain scopes).

Data model (simple):
- approval_token: token_id | token_payload_base64 | token_hash | issued_by | issued_at | expires_at | scope | reason | signature
- revocation_record: token_id | revoked_by | revoked_at | reason | revocation_receipt_hash | propagation_state
- evidence_bundle: token_id | token_hash | summary_blob_url | index_keys | retention_tier

Retention and compliance knobs:
- Customer default retention options: 90d (default for startup customers), 365d (enterprise), forever (legal hold).
- Export API: bulk export of evidence bundles for a time range + token scope. Support signed-URL delivery to customer S3.
- Jurisdictional hold: if customer requests data residency or has legal hold, route full logs to their provisioned S3 region and mark in ledger.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (experiment): implement token model + revoke API + Console dev button behind feature flag. Internal-only. 4 weeks.
- Phase 1 (beta): push webhook propagation to edge proxies for a subset of customers, expose TTL presets and revocation UI. 8 weeks.
- Phase 2 (ga): acked propagation mode and retention policies in Console + export + docs + runbooks. 12–16 weeks.

Monitoring & SLOs:
- Issuance latency p50 < 200ms, p99 < 1s.
- Revoke-to-edge propagation median < 2s for best-effort, acked ack < 5s for opted-in customers.
- Console query 99th percentile < 500ms for recent approvals.

Open questions / unresolved items (quick list):
- TTL maxima: should we allow >72h for automation flows? risk tradeoffs.
- Replay protection at edge: how to prevent replay if webhook delivery is intermittent? nonce? sequence numbers?
- How tightly to couple approval tokens with existing change_ids (gitops/pr flows)? recommend a mapping but allow loose coupling initially.
- Retention cost modeling: need finance estimates for 90/365/forever.
- UX: extend TTL vs reissue — require re-approval flow with second approver? configurable per-customer.

Security notes / threat model snippets:
- Tokens must be short-lived; store only hashes in main index for extra safety. Avoid storing token plaintext wherever possible.
- Revocation receipts must be signed with control-plane key to prevent spoofing.
- Webhook endpoints: require TLS mutual-auth for enterprise customers.

Runbooks (emergency):
- If a token is misused, immediate steps: revoke token -> escalate to SRE -> trigger snapshot of edge controller state -> pull evidence bundle -> notify customer.
- Test scenario: simulated emergency revocation during network partition. Verify propagation and operator experience.

Next steps (owners):
- Engineering (Jonas): prototype token schema + validate endpoint. (PRIV-4123)
- Infra (Ravi): design small durable store for revocation receipts with low-latency index.
- Product (Asha, Evelyn): finalize TTL presets and fail-open/closed defaults; write customer-facing docs and runbook.
- Security (Marta): review threat model and signing schemes.

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Wireframe Console revoke UX and mobile revoke flow
- [ ] Implement API contract and add to openapi spec
- [ ] Add sample evidence bundle and size test (target <4KB)
- [ ] Cost estimate for retention tiers (ask finance)

Notes to self: keep evidence bundle minimal but searchable. prioritize propagation correctness over fancy crypto. iterate with two pilot customers (legal/reg infra teams) to validate retention/jurisdiction needs.

Related threads / tickets: see linked artifacts; also reference slack thread "#private-deploy-approvals" for pilot asks.

End of draft.
